name: Wide-Grip Pronated T-Bar Row
description: The wide-grip pronated T-bar row uses a wider than shoulder-width overhand grip on a T-bar or landmine setup, shifting emphasis toward the middle trapezius, rear deltoids, and rhomboids compared to the standard close-grip version. The pronated wide grip limits biceps involvement and demands greater scapular retraction strength to complete each repetition.

execution.starting_position: Straddle the T-bar machine or landmine bar. Grip the wide handles (or bar itself) pronated, hands wider than shoulder width. Hinge to 45 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: If a T-bar machine is used, set the chest pad appropriately. For a landmine, use a straight bar without a handle attachment.
steps: Step 1: Begin hinged with arms extended gripping the bar wide.
Step 2: Initiate by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Step 3: Row elbows back and wide — not tucked into the torso.
Step 4: At the top, hold 1 second with shoulder blades fully retracted.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale descending.
common_mistakes: Elbows tracking too close to the body — wide grip requires wide elbows
Excessive torso extension at the top — maintain the hinge
safety_considerations: Wide pronated grip increases wrist stress — ensure wrists are strong and healthy
Do not add excessive spinal extension to assist the row
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to elbows behind torso level.
coaching_cues: Drive the shoulder blades together, not just back
